citation: Henry, J. and Kok, C. (eds.) (2013). A macro stress testing framework for assessing systemic risks in the banking sector. ECB Occasional Paper No 152.

dedupe_keys.name: ecb top down macro stress testing framework for systemic risk in the banking sector occasional paper 152

description: This record describes the top-down macro stress testing framework that the European Central Bank developed to assess the solvency of euro area banks under adverse macroeconomic and financial scenarios. Its four pillars are macro-financial scenario design, translation of scenarios into bank risk parameters through top-down satellite models, including a Bayesian model approach, solvency calculations, and analysis of contagion and feedback, with reverse stress tests and a stock-take of insurance sector tools. It was documented by staff of the ECB Directorate General Financial Stability, edited by Jérôme Henry and Christoffer Kok, as ECB Occasional Paper 152 in October 2013, and was used in EU/IMF financial assistance programmes and in preparing the Single Supervisory Mechanism. The paper is a free PDF from the ECB and SSRN; reproduction needs the ECB's written authorisation, and the model code and supervisory data are not public. Caveats: it documents the 2013 framework, which has since been developed further, and it needs confidential bank data to run. For simulation it gives a documented method for linking macroeconomic shocks to bank losses and interbank contagion, useful for cascading failure and resilience studies of how infrastructure or disaster losses reach the financial system. It is related to the EBA EU-wide stress testing record in this catalogue, whose bottom-up results it was used to challenge.
